Add a sensor for "summation_delivered" attribute of the ZCL SmartEnergy metering cluster. Most of my devices support only `instanteneous_demand` and `summa_devlivered` attributes of the SmartEnergy 0x0702 ZCL cluster. If either of the attributes are not supported, then the entity is not created.

Can HA do kW to W and W to kW conversions? Originally these sensors where kW unit of measurement, but people wanted it to be in W. Can an entity have a kW "native UOM" and HA converting it to whatever the customization is set?

> Can HA do kW to W and W to kW conversions? Originally these sensors where kW unit of measurement, but people wanted it to be in W. Can an entity have a kW "native UOM" and HA converting it to whatever the customization is set?

I don't know. But [according to the forums, Wh and kWh both work](https://community.home-assistant.io/t/energy-management-in-home-assistant/326854/255).
Yeah, summation should be in kWh or Wh. Means, I need to update summation to be *h while instantaneous_demand stays at W
Summation uses kWh for uom==0 and channels specific for any other. Why is this wrong?

> 
> 
> Summation uses kWh for uom==0 and channels specific for any other. Why is this wrong?

In case of, e.g., uom==1: the unit should be m^3 for summation_delivered (i.e., a volume) and m^3/hour for instantaneous_demand (i.e., the rate with which the volume changes). I.e., for same reason as kW is wrong for summation_delivered for uom==0.
You are overwhelming my competencies here, so unfortunately I can't be of help, but it is great to see you at work on this topic!

I am finding a similar issue with a salus sp600.  My understanding is:
- If the device reports only power (W) and not energy (kWh), then it will not show up in HA's energy metering.
- It is up to each integration to support kWh.
- Currently ZHA smart plugs [report only one value per cluster](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/34090#issuecomment-612644864) which is W, so ZHA smart plugs don't appear.
- Possible solutions:
  - [Enable ZHA to report more than one sensor per cluster](https://github.com/zigpy/zha-device-handlers/issues/605) then add a kWh sensor.
  - [Change all ZHA smart plugs to report kWh instead of W](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/50471) 
  - Create a manual sensor that integrates W to get kWh.
  - Add a 'last_reset' = 1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00 in customizations (although this didn't work for me).

> * Currently ZHA smart plugs [report only one value per cluster](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/34090#issuecomment-612644864) which is W, so ZHA smart plugs don't appear.

review_comments:
Possibly you need 
`_device_class: str | None = DEVICE_CLASS_ENERGY`
maybe also 
`_unit = ENERGY_KILO_WATT_HOUR`
here.  When I connect to my device, the new metering sensor appears (great!), but it is displayed in W (should be Wh or kWh).
It is summation value. It cannot be KWh, can it?. And unit of measurement is W is set by zigbee channel.

ZCL Specs are confusing at times. Summation is:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5826160/134996036-2c797552-7148-4609-8ae6-0bd30dce0dde.png)

and unit of measurement attribute both indicates kWh and kW 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5826160/134996318-48164b7b-be24-450c-b738-0c162d81dc51.png)

I guess my questions then are:
1. is summation supposed to be kW*h or just kW?
2. In case this is a non electric meter (water, gas etc) is it still `DEVICE_CLASS_ENERGY`?

Summation is surely kWh rather than kW. Summing a series of kW readings together from one sensor would have no meaning. There has to be a time factor in the unit for it to represent energy.  So the new value reported as 5000000W on my device is presumably 5000kWh (or maybe 500kWh due to a scaling factor error somewhere).

If it is a smart energy sensor measuring summation, then I suppose the class will always be energy.

Gas can be measured in kWh but usually m^3 where I live.  It feels like water should be something else.
Ok, made the summation sensor a `kWh` UOM if is an electric measurement and ignore device specified formatting, otherwise fallback to the channel UOM and formatting

> 
> 
> If it is a smart energy sensor measuring summation, then I suppose the class will always be energy.
> 
> Gas can be measured in kWh but usually m^3 where I live. It feels like water should be something else.

Yes, gas and water consumption is typically measured by volume; e.g., in m^3. Gas consumption (of some gases) can also be measured in, e.g., kWh or J, but the conversion factor would depend on the type of gas. 

I suppose the issue here is that while HA defines different device classes for ENERGY and POWER which are suitable for electrical summation and demand measurements, respectively, HA does not seem to provide classes corresponding to VOLUME and FLOW, which could be used for gas and water. 

There is a GAS device class, but I am not sure if it correspond to volume or flow. Maybe it does not differentiate and differentiation for gas is by uom? Furthermore HA does not seem to provide a generic device class for electricity devices or water.
I don't see how _unique_id_suffix would be anything other than `None` here.  So I presume that gets assigned in superclass.  But in the ZhaEntity class you seem to do almost the same thing again.
It's assigned in subclasses when inherenting he entity class. See sensor.SmartEnergySummation class

Seems correct to me based on the [specification ](https://zigbeealliance.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/docs-07-5356-19-0zse-zigbee-smart-energy-profile-specification.pdf) p229.  Leak probably only meaningful for gas meters unless somehow they measure earth leakage (RCD).
